items.question: Two identical cars are traveling on a highway. Car A is moving at 60 mph and Car B is moving at 30 mph. How does the kinetic energy of Car A compare to Car B?
options: Car A has four times the kinetic energy of Car B
Car A has twice the kinetic energy of Car B
Both cars have the same kinetic energy
Car B has more kinetic energy
items.correct_answer: Car A has four times the kinetic energy of Car B
items.explanation: Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of speed (KE = ½mv²). Doubling the speed quadruples the kinetic energy.

items.question: Create a graph showing how kinetic energy changes as speed increases for a 1 kg object. Calculate the kinetic energy at speeds of 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 m/s using KE = ½mv². Describe the pattern you observe and explain what it means for vehicle safety.

rubric.4: Accurate calculations (0.5J, 2J, 4.5J, 8J, 12.5J), graph showing curved relationship, pattern identified as exponential/squared growth, safety implications discussed (higher speeds much more dangerous)
rubric.3: Correct calculations with graph and pattern explanation
rubric.2: Some calculations correct, pattern not fully explained

items.question: A 2 kg bowling ball and a 5 kg bowling ball are rolling at the same speed. Which has more kinetic energy?
options: The 5 kg ball because kinetic energy increases with mass
The 2 kg ball because lighter objects move faster
They have the same kinetic energy
items.correct_answer: The 5 kg ball because kinetic energy increases with mass
items.explanation: Kinetic energy depends on both mass and speed. At the same speed, an object with more mass has proportionally more kinetic energy.

items.question: A book sits on a shelf 2 meters high. Compared to the same book on a shelf 4 meters high, the lower book has:
items.explanation: Gravitational potential energy increases with height. An object higher above the ground has more potential energy because it can do more work when it falls.

items.question: Develop a model to explain how potential energy changes as a roller coaster moves along its track. Include: 1) Where potential energy is highest and lowest, 2) What happens to the energy as the coaster moves, 3) Why the first hill must be the tallest.

rubric.4: Complete model showing PE highest at top of hills, lowest at bottom, energy converts to kinetic and back, first hill tallest because some energy lost to friction
rubric.3: Good model with energy transformation and height relationship
rubric.2: Shows energy changes but explanation incomplete
rubric.1: Basic roller coaster drawing without energy analysis

items.question: A stretched rubber band has elastic potential energy. A compressed spring also has elastic potential energy. Create a model comparing these two systems. Show how potential energy is stored and released in each case.

rubric.4: Model shows both systems with explanation of elastic deformation storing energy, energy released when objects return to original shape, real-world applications
rubric.3: Both systems shown with energy storage and release
rubric.2: One system explained well or both incomplete
